card: This PR adds lightweight, thread-safe test assertion macros in test utilities to replace Boost test macros across unit and fuzz tests. The new macros abort immediately on failure to prevent noisy CI logs, operate cleanly under ThreadSanitizer, and reject mixed signedness comparisons at compile time. It converts streams_tests.cpp as a proof of concept. The PR is currently an experimental sketch marked NOMERGE.
evidence: PR description demonstrates silent comparison bugs under Boost: "BOOST_CHECK_GT(-10, 10U); compiles and passes fine, even though it is obviously wrong."
PR description highlights ThreadSanitizer incompatibilities: "The check macros are not thread-safe. Using them in a thread will compile fine, but then fail tsan later on."
PR references tracking issue #34666 for test framework improvements.
problem: Boost unit test macros cannot be reused in fuzz tests or other non-Boost harnesses, fail under ThreadSanitizer when called from secondary threads, and continue executing after failures, which creates noisy logs that obscure the root cause. Additionally, Boost macros silently permit unsafe mixed-signedness integer comparisons like `BOOST_CHECK_GT(-10, 10U)` to pass.

risk.why: Touches only unit test infrastructure and test suites, with no impact on node behavior or production binaries.

scope_notes: The PR is explicitly titled as a draft sketch ([NOMERGE,SKETCH]). The implementation relies on C++20 features including std::source_location, concepts, and std::ranges. Commit f86123e888 is a scripted diff converting streams_tests.cpp.
summary: Introduces custom assertion macros (`ASSERT`, `ASSERT_EQ`, `ASSERT_EQ_COLLECTIONS`, `ASSERT_EXCEPTION`, and comparison variants) in `src/test/util/common.h` as lightweight, thread-safe, and fail-fast replacements for Boost test check macros. The new helpers reject mixed-signedness comparisons at compile time, print detailed mismatch diagnostics using `std::source_location`, and immediately abort on failure. The PR converts `src/test/streams_tests.cpp` to validate the new macros.
